subject: Discovery Recap: Inference Cost Reduction for FinBot
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samir Shah <samir@finbot.ai>, Ava Khan <ava@finbot.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Feb 2026 16:20:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery Recap: Inference Cost Reduction for FinBot

Samir / Ava — thanks for taking the time today. Short recap from our call and proposed next steps so we have alignment.

Pain points & goals
- Unit economics: inference cost per active user is the single biggest blocker for your pricing model. Current infra costs ~ $0.045/token on average for peak flows. You need to get closer to $0.01–$0.02/token for sustainable margins.
- Latency sensitivity: many flows have <500ms p95 requirement; heavy tail from long-context sessions.
- Operational predictability: predictable monthly spend and a path to dedicated capacity for production.

Current stack & constraints
- Frontend: product accepts user prompts via Kafka queue -> microservice -> hosted LLM endpoints (open-models + proprietary).
- You currently use single-GPU hosted endpoints with minimal batching; KV-cache not used widely.
- Quantization: engineering open to 4-bit if quality checks pass; legal wants documentation for model fidelity tests.

Success criteria (what would make this a win)
- 40–60% reduction in per-token inference cost at parity-quality for core flows.
- p95 latency <= 500ms for short prompts and reasonable tail for long contexts.
- Transparent cost breakdown to report to finance and product.

Immediate next steps
1) Redwood to share a ballpark pricing estimate and a short MA (mutual action) plan for a 6–8 week POC — Ben will attach the pricing sheet. (Ben: can you add a few capacity/config scenarios?)
2) Schedule tech deep dive with engineering to validate KV caching and batching plan (Ben + engineering). Propose window next Tue/Wed.
3) FinBot to share a few anonymized sample prompts/traffic profile and token distribution (we can accept sanitized CSV).

Open items
- Quantization acceptance criteria: define evaluation set and allowable quality delta.
- Procurement timeline & contracts — Monica from Redwood will assist with procurement steps.

Attachments: FinBot_MA_Plan_v1.pdf (overview, 3 pages)

Thanks again — I’ll follow up with the pricing estimate and proposed calendar invite for the tech deep-dive.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0182

Note: This thread contains summary notes from a call on 2026-02-15 between Redwood and FinBot. Internal participants are Rebecca/Ben/Monica as needed for follow-up.

From: Samir Shah <samir@finbot.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Ava Khan <ava@finbot.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery Recap: Inference Cost Reduction for FinBot

Thanks Marissa — good summary. A few clarifications from our side: 
- The $0.045/token figure is an average across mixed models; core user-facing flows (chat + doc retrieval) are the highest cost. We can extract token distributions and send by EOD Wed.
- We're definitely open to 4-bit quantization for the customer-facing pipeline, provided we can run an A/B over a week and see <2% delta on intent accuracy.
- For latency: some of our short prompts are extremely latency-sensitive (search/assistant interactions). If batching increases p95 beyond 500ms for those flows, we need policies to route them to lower-latency pools.

Next steps we confirm:
1) We'll send sanitized token distribution and a short list of representative prompts (by 18 Feb).
2) Please send the pricing estimate + MA plan. We’ll review internally and loop procurement.

Also looping in Ava (CTO) on the timeline. Thanks — looking forward.

—Samir

Subject: Re: Discovery Recap: Inference Cost Reduction for FinBot

Samir — thanks. Attached is a first-pass pricing estimate and three POC configurations:
- Config A (hosted, conservative): small batching + prefix caching; 20% cost reduction estimate.
- Config B (hosted + caching + aggressive batching): 45% cost reduction estimate; requires warm KV cache and some request shaping.
- Config C (dedicated capacity, quantized 4-bit): 60%+ cost reduction estimate; requires dedicated pool and initial calibration run.

Attachment: redwood-inference-pricing-estimate.xlsx (spreadsheet, 48 KB)

Proposed tech deep-dive slots:
- Wed 18 Feb 10:00–11:00 PT (Ben + infra eng)
- Wed 18 Feb 15:00–16:00 PT (Ben + infra eng)

We’ll prepare a short runbook on how batching and KV caching would be integrated into your pipeline (Kafka consumer -> Redwood SDK client -> routing policy). Also will include quantization test plan and evaluation metrics for the A/B.

Monica — can you add procurement/contract checklist and expected timeline to the MA plan?

Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
